# Koîos, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Koîos** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Koîos has no independent mythic biography; he exists in the genealogies and in the shadow of the Titanomachy. Yet his name and offspring give him a quiet importance. Hesiod names Koîos as a son of Ouranos and Gaia, brother of Kronos, Rhea, and the other Titans.  He married his sister Phoebe, 'Bright', and fathered Leto and Asteria.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Koîos
- **ASCII form:** coeus
- **Meaning:** "Questioning, inquiry"
- **Domain of influence:** Titan of Intellect
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Κοῖος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 59 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Κοῖος**. On the evidence, it means "Questioning, inquiry".

**Koîos** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *coeus* and **Koîos** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Koîos** lives at [/sites/coeus/](/sites/coeus/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/coeus/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/coeus/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/coeus/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Koîos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **AI, Data & Predictive Intelligence** — Questioning and inquiry personified; the Titan of the query.
- **Education, Research & Knowledge** — Intellect and inquiry; research as a divine act.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — Through Leto he is grandfather of Apollo and Artemis; the Delphic line descends from him.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
